answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making every vote stake-backed: each identity posts a bond and may attest only once, and conflicting attestations slash that bond. The network checks that a signature belongs to a bonded identity, so a clone carries no weight until its owner pays real money. An attacker flooding the ocean with fake agents must fund one bond per vote, and any double-vote burns the deposit. Like a plume scattered by the tide, the expense grows with every lie: swaying a thousand votes means risking a thousand bonds, so the attack becomes self-defeating.
